In spite of these hardships the Med'ja had stood resolute and for their faith they had been rewarded, for while they had rediscovered old enemies they had also made new friends. A small contingent of Saean, beckoned forth by the Goddesses Pomme and Zille had emerged bearing gifts as they travelled southward to visit their kin. They had brought with them a plant unlike any the Med'ja had seen before, it appeared to possess a mind of its own swaying to and fro as it sought a hold within its surroundings. The plant, the Saean claimed, could be taught and trained so that it might grow to house and protect the fledgling tribe from the dangers of the forest.

Lo'te, Ma'te and the council of Elders thought long into the night as they considered the gift left by the Saean. Why had the Gods driven them from their home and then provided them with such a gift? Surely a plant such as this could have provided much protection against the beasts that claimed the lighstone by disguising the entrance to the Burrows. The Gods must be taunting them. Sohti'le, shaman of the cult of Umbralocht spoke first "For years our tribe prospered beneath the earth but this was not always our way. Once our ancestors lived among the trees as we do now, living and dying in balance with the creatures of the forest, the forest has grown wild in our absence dear brothers and sisters; the beast was not a curse but a warning from the Gods; a call to retake our place among the creatures of the surface. The plant is a gift for accepting the will of the Gods"

The council bickered over the Shaman's words until just before sunrise when the twin rules rose and spoke as one "Enough! Our situation is dire, our people in need, whether for good or evil the Gods have provided us with a solution to our plight and we will not allow fear to rule us again. We will take this gift and learn from it what we can, if it is a boon then we shall use it, if not then we shall destroy it. So say we, the twin Chieftains of the Med'ja-Hom'te
